candidates.name: Precise exception handling and failure propagation
candidates.kind: Existing tool plus bespoke control-flow rule
candidates.rules: Ruff BLE001; proposed no-success-after-failure rule
candidates.gap: BLE and TRY are not selected. B904 already covers exception chaining; it does not prevent swallowed failures.
candidates.enforcement: Enable BLE001; separately reject a failed job path that logs an exception then returns an ordinary success value. Preserve explicit failure outcomes or re-raise.
candidates.example: Reject `except Exception: return 0`; also inspect `logging.exception(...); return 0`, which BLE001 permits.
candidates.oracle: An expected failure remains a failure through the job boundary; successful and deliberate recovery paths still work.
candidates.risk: Legitimate top-level cleanup/recovery exists. BLE001 alone is insufficient: its logging exemption passed the isolated probe.
candidates.cost: Low for BLE001; medium for scoped control-flow analysis.
candidates.status: Pinned Ruff differential probe confirms additional coverage and its limit.

candidates.name: Timezone-aware forecast instants
candidates.kind: Existing tool
candidates.rules: Ruff DTZ001–DTZ007, DTZ011–DTZ012 as applicable
candidates.gap: DTZ is absent. Forecast cut-offs require unambiguous instants, not implicit machine-local time.
candidates.enforcement: Select the supported DTZ rules for code handling instants; define explicit conversion at ingestion boundaries.
candidates.example: Reject `datetime.now()` for a forecast instant; require an explicit timezone such as UTC.
candidates.oracle: Naive construction fails lint; aware instants pass; time-zone boundary tests preserve the same instant.
candidates.risk: Calendar dates and local wall-clock business values can be valid. Distinguish their types rather than misclassifying every date as an instant.
candidates.cost: Low static cost; temporal semantics still need tests.
candidates.status: Pinned Ruff probe flagged the naive clock that current configuration accepts.

candidates.name: Effect ownership and canonical API access
candidates.kind: Existing tool plus bespoke boundary rule
candidates.rules: Ruff TID251 configured bans; proposed EFFECT_OWNER contract
candidates.gap: Current architecture permits all standard-library imports in pure layers, including network/process/file APIs. Layer direction alone is not effect isolation.
candidates.enforcement: Restrict known IO APIs and client construction to owned adapters/entrypoints; use symbol-aware matching. State which dynamic imports are allowed.
candidates.example: A domain import of `urllib.request.urlopen` passes the current layer check; a configured TID251 rule rejects it with an adapter-directed message.
candidates.oracle: Known IO calls in domain/application fail; the same approved capability in its adapter passes; aliases are covered.
candidates.risk: Pure path manipulation is not file IO. Do not ban all pathlib use or claim syntactic matching detects every dynamic effect.
candidates.cost: Low for explicit APIs; medium for typed/call-aware ownership checks.
candidates.status: Confirmed by a static differential fixture; no network call was executed.

candidates.name: No unchecked Any crossing a typed boundary
candidates.kind: Existing type checker plus runtime validation
candidates.rules: Mypy disallow_any_explicit/disallow_any_unimported; scoped disallow_any_expr; validated decoders
candidates.gap: Mypy strict is not a ban on every Any expression. JSON-derived values can flow into an annotated variable without runtime validation.
candidates.enforcement: Validate external payloads in adapters, expose narrow typed ports, and apply stronger Any checks in owned core code. Treat cast as an assertion, not parsing.
candidates.example: Current mypy accepts `payload=json.loads(text); runner_id: int=payload['runner_id']`; scoped disallow_any_expr rejects the unchecked flow.
candidates.oracle: Wrong input shapes are rejected at the boundary; valid decoded objects enter the core without Any; typed SDK paths remain usable.
candidates.risk: Blanket Any-expression bans across dynamic third-party libraries can create casts or wrapper sprawl. Calibrate scope before making a blocking rule.
candidates.cost: Low-to-medium incremental type-check cost; runtime validation per boundary.
candidates.status: Pinned mypy 1.19.1 differential probe confirms the gap.

candidates.name: Whole-package cycles and protected interfaces
candidates.kind: Existing tool
candidates.rules: Import Linter acyclic_siblings; protected/independence contracts where justified
candidates.gap: Per-file allowed-layer checks do not detect cycles within an allowed layer or package-level feedback loops.
candidates.enforcement: Add a whole-package cycle contract at the existing package root; preserve current dependency direction. Add explicit internal APIs rather than duplicating existing layer checks.
candidates.example: Two domain modules can mutually import while both satisfy the current allowed-layer map.
candidates.oracle: A same-layer cycle fails and its acyclic counterpart passes; diagnostics show the edge/cycle path.
candidates.risk: Do not install permissive generic layer defaults, missing optional layers or ignore_imports to make the result green. Dynamic imports need a separate policy.
candidates.cost: Whole-package graph construction; benchmark once the codebase grows.
candidates.status: Import Linter 2.15 failed the synthetic cycle and passed the repaired graph.

candidates.name: Dependency declaration and runtime/dev separation
candidates.kind: Existing tool
candidates.rules: Deptry DEP001–DEP004
candidates.gap: The foundation deliberately installs tooling/runtime services in a dev environment. A future production package must not rely on transitively installed or dev-only libraries.
candidates.enforcement: Check direct, missing, unused and misplaced dependencies in production source; verify the production artifact without development dependencies.
candidates.example: Importing a library only because MLflow happens to install it should fail the production dependency contract.
candidates.oracle: A package with only its declared runtime dependencies can execute its owned journey; removing a required direct dependency is detected.
candidates.risk: CLI-only dev tools are not unused runtime dependencies. Dynamic plugins and namespace packages require an explicit discovery contract.
candidates.cost: Low-to-medium source/environment inspection.
candidates.status: Maintained tool documented; no full-repository Deptry run or production packaging claim made.

candidates.name: Exception tests that cannot pass at the wrong statement
candidates.kind: Existing tool
candidates.rules: Ruff PT011 and PT012
candidates.gap: Pytest bypass checks exist, but PT rules are not selected. A broad raises block can succeed because setup failed rather than the intended operation.
candidates.enforcement: Require a specific exception expectation and a single raising operation in the context; assert useful failure meaning without exact incidental message snapshots.
candidates.example: Move fixture setup outside `pytest.raises`; make the contract operation the only statement expected to raise.
candidates.oracle: Wrong failure reasons and setup failures do not satisfy the scenario; the intended rejected behaviour does.
candidates.risk: Iterator/context-manager edge cases exist. Preserve behaviour-focused scenarios instead of one test per assertion.
candidates.cost: Low.
candidates.status: Supported stable rules verified in the installed Ruff catalog.

candidates.name: Structured, stable job diagnostics
candidates.kind: Existing tool plus bespoke record-schema checks
candidates.rules: Ruff G004; proposed structured-event schema
candidates.gap: T20 already rejects print, but no rule establishes structured job/run/dataset/model context or consistent failure events.
candidates.enforcement: Use one event schema and owned logger adapter; validate required correlation fields and error status. G004 catches eager interpolated logging, not the schema itself.
candidates.example: Use a stable event name and structured identifiers instead of embedding the entire job context in an f-string.
candidates.oracle: A failed job emits a valid failure record with traceable identifiers, without exposing secret values.
candidates.risk: A logger call is not evidence that a failure propagated; avoid assuming G004 enforces structured logging or secret redaction.
candidates.cost: Low static check plus focused record validation.
candidates.status: Capability documented; project-specific event contract remains to be designed.

candidates.name: Unused definitions and unreachable subgraphs
candidates.kind: Existing tool plus graph concept
candidates.rules: Vulture; declared-root graph reachability
candidates.gap: F401/F841 and ARG cover imports/locals/arguments, but not every abandoned public function, plugin or disconnected feature subtree.
candidates.enforcement: Combine declared entrypoints with whole-source reachability and review Vulture findings; delete only after real usage paths are accounted for.
candidates.example: A never-referenced feature module with internal imports can escape a simple orphan test; root reachability can expose it.
candidates.oracle: Registered entrypoints/plugins remain admitted; an intentionally unreferenced fixture is found.
candidates.risk: Vulture's lower-confidence labels are heuristics, not calibrated probabilities. High-confidence results overlap existing gates; public-definition findings need review.
candidates.cost: Low-to-medium; whole-source graph needed for disconnected files.
candidates.status: Do not enable blanket deletion or convert every finding to a blocking gate.

candidates.name: Duplicate logic and semantic contract drift
candidates.kind: Existing detector plus bespoke contract comparison
candidates.rules: jscpd clone detection; proposed canonical-contract comparison
candidates.gap: No clone detector or canonical schema/value drift check exists; copied feature or publication logic can diverge while each copy passes lint.
candidates.enforcement: Use clone reports to locate candidates, then test shared invariants or generate repeated schemas from one source.
candidates.example: Two copies of odds conversion or feature-order definitions evolve separately; centralize their contract only when they share the same responsibility.
candidates.oracle: A deliberate divergent copy is reported; legitimate boilerplate does not force a misleading abstraction.
candidates.risk: Similarity is not semantic identity. Avoid zero-duplication gates and aggressive auto-refactors that merge unrelated concepts.
candidates.cost: Repository-wide token comparison; calibrate thresholds on meaningful examples.
candidates.status: Active project evidence; detector not benchmarked or installed as a gate here.

candidates.name: Coupling and change-impact budgets
candidates.kind: Transferable design with bespoke graph metrics
candidates.rules: Dependency-cruiser moreUnstable concept; WPS module/import/member complexity concepts
candidates.gap: Current complexity thresholds are mostly local to functions. They do not measure how many modules a change can affect.
candidates.enforcement: Report fan-in/fan-out, strongly connected components and transitive change reach; calibrate any hard budget by component role.
candidates.example: A small helper importing many unrelated subsystems can have low local complexity and high change impact.
candidates.oracle: A cross-domain coupling fixture expands the reported impact set; a composition root is recognized as a different role.
candidates.risk: Dependency instability is not a verdict of bad code. Raw import counts can be gamed by namespace imports or extra wrapper modules.
candidates.cost: Graph-wide analysis; no fixed latency or change-effort savings claimed.
candidates.status: Conceptual adaptation; no threshold is recommended as empirically optimal for agents.

candidates.name: Reject stateless wrapper classes without a role
candidates.kind: Cross-language concept with bespoke AST rule
candidates.rules: typescript-eslint no-extraneous-class concept
candidates.gap: Python object-choice guidance is prose; generic-name checks do not detect unnecessary class-only namespaces.
candidates.enforcement: Flag classes used solely as static namespaces for review; use functions/modules unless state, lifecycle, polymorphism or a data contract justifies a class.
candidates.example: A class containing only static utility functions can add ceremony without owning behaviour or state.
candidates.oracle: Stateless namespace wrappers are found; dataclasses, Protocols, Enums, exceptions and framework-required classes remain valid.
candidates.risk: One public method is not automatically a smell. A universal minimum-method rule would reject legitimate domain objects.
candidates.cost: Low AST cost, but scope requires careful semantic exclusions.
candidates.status: Do not port the TypeScript implementation mechanically to Python.

candidates.name: Leakage and forecast-time dataset contracts
candidates.kind: Bespoke static guard plus runtime/data checks
candidates.rules: Declared split/cut-off API; dataset availability and partition invariants
candidates.gap: No real training dataset exists yet. Generic lint cannot know whether a feature was available at forecast time or whether all runners stay with their race.
candidates.enforcement: Own the split/feature APIs, prohibit raw split/label access outside them, and validate availability times, complete-race partitions and untouched holdouts on real manifests.
candidates.example: Fitting preprocessing on the combined dataset before splitting must fail an outcome check; a naive spelling-based lint can miss aliased calls.
candidates.oracle: Temporal leakage, race overlap and repeated holdout use are rejected; an agreed valid snapshot passes.
candidates.risk: Static leakage tools have library/notebook scope limits. Do not claim full leakage freedom from a general AST linter.
candidates.cost: Static checks can be cheap; complete dataset invariants scale with data and belong at the appropriate pipeline boundary.
candidates.status: Research tools inform design; not a turnkey CI recommendation for this script/container pipeline.

candidates.name: Explicit dataframe mutation boundaries
candidates.kind: Existing tool and immutable-data design
candidates.phase: If pandas is selected for features
candidates.rules: Ruff PD002; explicit transformation ownership
candidates.gap: PD rules are absent. The repository has Arrow artifacts but has not selected the feature-processing API.
candidates.enforcement: Where pandas is used, prefer explicit returned transformations; keep shared snapshots immutable by contract.
candidates.example: Prefer an assigned transformed frame over `inplace=True` on a shared frame.
candidates.oracle: An input snapshot is unchanged by a feature transform; the transformed output satisfies its schema.
candidates.risk: PD002 does not detect every mutation and is not needed merely because pandas is an MLflow dependency.
candidates.cost: Low static cost; mutation outcome checks on representative data.
candidates.status: Conditional on actual pandas use, not a reason to introduce pandas.

candidates.name: Typed model lifecycle and exhaustive state handling
candidates.kind: Cross-language concept plus existing type checks
candidates.rules: Mypy exhaustive-match; protected construction of validated/approved objects
candidates.gap: Approval and publication are not implemented. Boolean flags and generic dictionaries would allow ambiguous transitions and multiply change sites.
candidates.enforcement: Represent lifecycle states explicitly and make publication require the approved-state contract produced by the owned approval boundary.
candidates.example: Adding a new model state should make incomplete dispatch fail; a raw candidate should not satisfy the publication interface.
candidates.oracle: Unapproved and failed candidates cannot publish; every declared state has explicit handling and runtime authorization remains enforced.
candidates.risk: Types can be forged with casts and dataclass freezing is shallow. Static checks do not replace real approval authorization or persisted evidence.
candidates.cost: Low static cost plus state-transition and authorization tests.
candidates.status: Optional mypy code exists in 1.19.1; full lifecycle design is proposed, not implemented.

candidates.name: Semantic SQL extraction guard
candidates.kind: Bespoke rule using an existing parser
candidates.rules: SQLGlot AST policy plus PostgreSQL read-only privileges
candidates.gap: SQLFluff checks SQL form and selected conventions; a read-only fixture exists, but no production extraction SQL policy is implemented.
candidates.enforcement: Parse the chosen dialect and reject disallowed statement/CTE operations; retain real read-only database roles and transaction constraints.
candidates.example: A WITH clause containing a modifying statement must not pass merely because a query ends in SELECT.
candidates.oracle: Disallowed write forms fail static checks and real database write attempts fail; permitted extraction remains usable.
candidates.risk: A SELECT can call a side-effecting function. Parsing alone cannot establish privilege, function behaviour or resource safety.
candidates.cost: Low-to-medium parsing plus the existing real-service seam extended for the owned adapter.
candidates.status: Parser capability inspected; proposed application policy not coded.

candidates.name: GitHub Actions security invariants
candidates.kind: Existing tool
candidates.rules: Zizmor artipacked, template-injection, excessive-permissions, dangerous-triggers, unpinned-uses
candidates.gap: actionlint/YAML validate syntax and selected shell issues, but do not establish these security invariants.
candidates.enforcement: Add a pinned, strict-collection security scan. Review checkout credential persistence and future workflow privilege/trigger changes.
candidates.example: Both existing checkout steps omit `persist-credentials: false`.
candidates.oracle: A risky workflow fixture produces a nonzero gate result; a reviewed safe fixture passes; collection errors cannot disappear.
candidates.risk: The actual probe found two medium-severity, low-confidence artipacked findings, not proven leaks. Online audits have different capabilities and prerequisites.
candidates.cost: Low offline scan in this small workflow set; online audits require separate setup.
candidates.status: Read-only zizmor 1.30.1 probe completed; no autofix or gate change.

candidates.name: PostgreSQL migration lock and rewrite safety
candidates.kind: Existing tool
candidates.phase: Only if this repository owns schema migrations
candidates.rules: Squawk require-concurrent-index-creation, constraint-missing-not-valid, prefer-timestamptz and related rules
candidates.gap: SQL formatting is not migration safety. The ML repository currently does not own Nexus schema changes.
candidates.enforcement: Apply migration-aware rules in the repository that owns the DDL, with version-appropriate PostgreSQL semantics and rehearsal.
candidates.example: Flag an index build that unnecessarily blocks writes; keep concurrent index creation outside a transaction where PostgreSQL requires it.
candidates.oracle: Unsafe migration fixtures are rejected and the reviewed migration executes under realistic locking conditions.
candidates.risk: Rules are not blanket bans: fresh empty tables differ from populated production tables. Do not add Nexus write authority to this project.
candidates.cost: Low static cost; real migration rehearsal is separate.
candidates.status: Deferred unless migration ownership becomes part of scope.

candidates.name: Rendered infrastructure policy
candidates.kind: Existing policy engine or bespoke typed checks
candidates.rules: Conftest/Rego or equivalent Python policy over rendered Compose and Terraform plan JSON
candidates.gap: Current tests protect a specific storage module and static files. They do not yet enforce every future resource or resolved local service configuration.
candidates.enforcement: Check effective settings: expected image identity, no unapproved privilege/socket mounts, allowed cloud scope, approved resource types and workload-specific permissions.
candidates.example: A harmless-looking override must not render a privileged container or an unintended cloud target.
candidates.oracle: Unsafe rendered fixtures fail; missing/unknown required values fail explicitly; planned environment differences pass by contract.
candidates.risk: Rego adds a language/toolchain. A small Python policy may be simpler; do not stack overlapping scanners without an identified new invariant.
candidates.cost: Low-to-medium policy evaluation; cloud plan generation has separate credentials/state boundaries.
candidates.status: Proposed semantic layer, not a claim that present configuration is unsafe.

candidates.name: Handle every asynchronous result
candidates.kind: Cross-language concept plus existing type checker
candidates.rules: Mypy unused-awaitable; existing default unused-coroutine retained
candidates.gap: A discarded generic Awaitable can pass current strict mypy even though ordinary unused coroutines already have checking.
candidates.enforcement: Require awaiting, returning or explicitly owned task lifecycle management; introduce async-specific library lint only when that library is used.
candidates.example: Calling a function returning Awaitable[int] and discarding it passes baseline but fails with unused-awaitable enabled.
candidates.oracle: Discarded work is rejected; managed tasks demonstrate completion/cancellation/error handling.
candidates.risk: Merely assigning or discarding into a named variable is not lifecycle ownership. TypeScript's void escape illustrates why syntactic silencing is insufficient.
candidates.cost: Low incremental type-check cost.
candidates.status: Confirmed in pinned mypy differential fixture; project currently has no async pipeline.

candidates.name: One source for contracts and feature order
candidates.kind: Bespoke deterministic comparison
candidates.rules: Canonical schema/manifest generation and parity checks
candidates.gap: Exact wording is required in guidance, but no executable parity contract yet binds dataset schema, feature order, model metadata and publication payload.
candidates.enforcement: Generate or compare repeated representations from one owned contract, with explicit version/hash linkage.
candidates.example: A feature-order change must invalidate an incompatible model manifest instead of silently reusing the old artifact.
candidates.oracle: A deliberate contract mismatch is rejected; changing the canonical contract updates every dependent generated representation.
candidates.risk: Do not infer semantic equality from similar strings or merge distinct concepts such as starting price and editorial forecast price.
candidates.cost: Low metadata checks; integration outcomes still need the real pipeline seam.
candidates.status: Proposed future invariant; field names and acceptance thresholds still need domain agreement.

candidates.name: Behavioural properties for gates and ML transformations
candidates.kind: Existing test generator; complementary to lint
candidates.phase: Gate changes and first feature slice
candidates.rules: Hypothesis properties and targeted mutation-style challenges
candidates.gap: Example-based verifier tests are valuable, but coverage alone cannot prove resistance to aliases, nesting variants, false success or ML leakage.
candidates.enforcement: Generate valid/invalid structures and data partitions; test invariant preservation rather than exact source text or one discovered value.
candidates.example: Reordering runners should not change race membership; an aliased forbidden call should remain rejected.
candidates.oracle: Meaningfully different invalid cases fail while equivalent valid cases pass; production code is included in appropriate coverage when introduced.
candidates.risk: Generators can mirror implementation mistakes. Keep an independent behavioural oracle and the single real-service seam.
candidates.cost: Bounded fast property tests; expensive journey checks remain explicitly invoked.
candidates.status: Complementary verification, not presented as a static lint rule.

candidates.name: Gate result and scanner-coverage contracts
candidates.kind: Bespoke integration assertions
candidates.rules: Failing-exit, nonempty intended scope, unknown-result and suppression-policy checks
candidates.gap: Existing guards reject many bypasses, but adding another tool introduces new output formats, ignores, baselines and collection failure modes.
candidates.enforcement: Test the wrapper with known findings, scanner errors and omitted inputs; map each maintained executable location to its checker.
candidates.example: Zizmor SARIF output can accompany exit zero despite findings; use a verified blocking path instead of equating upload success with safety.
candidates.oracle: The end-to-end gate fails on a known violation and an analysis failure; empty scope is accepted only when explicitly expected for the project phase.
candidates.risk: Do not confuse source-type admission with actual scanner coverage or auto-ignore generated reports by broad unreviewed patterns.
candidates.cost: Small integration tests; no need to rerun the entire slow journey for each lint edit.
candidates.status: Required integration discipline; no existing gate was changed during this research.
